overview: Binary Tree GATE ka sabse bada single DS topic hai (53 PYQs). 7 sub-skills: traversal-based tree reconstruction, node-counting formulas (leaf/internal/degree relationships), height-vs-node-count bounds, array-representation index formulas, tree-recursion code tracing, balanced-tree operations, aur structure/deletion design.
whyItMatters: Har saal multiple questions guaranteed. BST aur Binary Heap dono isi foundation pe bane hain.
coreConcept: Binary Tree = har node ke max 2 children (left, right). 3 standard traversals: Preorder (Root-Left-Right), Inorder (Left-Root-Right), Postorder (Left-Right-Root). SABSE IMPORTANT FACT: Inorder + (Preorder YA Postorder) mil ke tree UNIQUELY reconstruct kar sakte hain — lekin sirf Preorder+Postorder (bina Inorder ke) UNIQUE NAHI hota (unless tree strictly full/binary with specific constraints).
hinglishExplanation: Traversal ko ek 'ghoomne ka order' socho — Root pehle dekhna hai ya baad me, aur Left pehle ya Right pehle, yehi teeno traversals decide karte hain. Reconstruction ka trick: INORDER tumhe batata hai 'kaun LEFT me hai, kaun RIGHT me hai' (root ke around split karke), aur PREORDER/POSTORDER tumhe batata hai 'ROOT kaun hai' har step pe. Dono milke recursively pura tree build kar sakte ho.
formalDefinition: A binary tree node has at most 2 children (left, right). Full binary tree: every node has 0 or 2 children. Complete binary tree: all levels full except possibly the last, filled left to right. Perfect binary tree: all internal nodes have 2 children AND all leaves at the same level.
importantProperties: Inorder+Preorder OR Inorder+Postorder together ALWAYS uniquely reconstruct the tree.
Preorder+Postorder alone does NOT uniquely reconstruct a general binary tree (though it DOES work for a strictly-full binary tree where every node has 0 or 2 children).
For a binary tree where EVERY node has 0 or 2 children (full binary tree): (number of leaves) = (number of internal/2-degree nodes) + 1. This n=2L-1 style relationship is tested constantly.
Maximum nodes in a binary tree of height h (edges) = 2^(h+1) - 1. Minimum nodes in a tree of height h = h+1 (a pure skewed chain).
A complete binary tree with n nodes stored in an array (1-indexed): parent of node i = i/2 (floor), left child = 2i, right child = 2i+1. (0-indexed shifts these by 1.)

Number of binary trees possible with n unlabeled nodes = Catalan number C(n) = (2n)!/((n+1)!n!). With n LABELED/distinct-valued nodes arranged as BSTs, it's the SAME Catalan count (only one valid BST shape per Catalan-tree-shape, since BST order is forced).

formulas.leafInternalRelationFullTree: In a binary tree where every node has 0 or 2 children: L (leaves) = I (internal, 2-children nodes) + 1, and total nodes n = 2L-1 = 2I+1
formulas.degreeSumFormula: For any tree: (nodes of degree 1) + 2×(nodes of degree 2) = n - 1 (sum of degrees = 2×edges = 2(n-1) for a tree with n nodes, since a tree has n-1 edges); also n = n0+n1+n2 (degree-0/1/2 counts) and edges = n1+2·n2 = n-1
formulas.maxNodesHeight: Max nodes in binary tree of height h (edges) = 2^(h+1) - 1
formulas.minNodesHeight: Min nodes in binary tree of height h (edges) = h + 1
formulas.arrayRepParentChild: 1-indexed complete binary tree in array: parent(i)=⌊i/2⌋, left(i)=2i, right(i)=2i+1
formulas.catalanTreeCount: Number of distinct binary tree SHAPES with n nodes = Catalan number C(n) = (2n)!/((n+1)!n!)

keyPropertiesAndIdentities: The n0 = n2 + 1 relationship (leaf count = 2-degree-node count + 1) is DERIVED from: n = n0+n1+n2 AND edges = n-1 = n1+2n2 → combine to eliminate n1 and get n0=n2+1. Memorize the RESULT, but know you can re-derive it if needed.
'Weighted/total external path length' = Σ(depth of each leaf × its weight) — used in optimal merge/Huffman-coding-adjacent contexts.
commonPitfalls: Assuming Preorder+Postorder ALONE uniquely determines a tree — it only does so for strictly full (0-or-2-children) binary trees, not general ones.

Height defined as 'number of EDGES' vs 'number of NODES' on longest root-to-leaf path — GATE questions specify one or the other; always check which definition is being used (off-by-one errors are extremely common here).
Confusing 0-indexed vs 1-indexed array formulas for complete-binary-tree parent/child relationships.
Forgetting the n0=n2+1 relationship applies ONLY to trees where every node has 0 or 2 children (not general binary trees where degree-1 nodes exist).
standardTechniques: For reconstruction: find the ROOT from preorder (first element) or postorder (last element), then use INORDER to split remaining nodes into left-subtree-set and right-subtree-set, recurse.
For counting-relationship questions: set up n0+n1+n2=n and n1+2n2=n-1 (or the equivalent for your tree's degree definition) and solve algebraically rather than memorizing every derived formula.
For height/node-count bound questions: always clarify edge-count vs node-count height definition FIRST, before applying 2^(h+1)-1 style formulas.
For code-tracing on tree-recursive functions: draw the actual tree, trace the recursive calls bottom-up from leaves exactly like the Recursion topic's call-tree method.
